title: World Development Report 2018: Learning to Realize Education's Promise
description: Flagship World Bank report documenting the global learning crisis, finding that schooling does not always lead to learning, and proposing a three-pronged strategy focused on assessing learning, acting on evidence, and aligning actors to make schools work for all learners.

title: The Effect of Girls' Education on Health Outcomes: Fact Sheet
description: Overview of evidence on the relationship between girls' education and development outcomes, showing that each additional year of schooling for girls reduces child mortality, increases future earnings, and lowers rates of child marriage.

title: Making Schools Work: New Evidence on Accountability Reforms
authors: Barbara Bruns, Deon Filmer, Harry Anthony Patrinos
description: World Bank report examining accountability-based education reforms in developing countries, analyzing evidence on school-based management, teacher accountability, school choice, and performance-based incentives across multiple country contexts.

title: Expanding Opportunities for the Next Generation: Early Childhood Development in the Middle East and North Africa
description: Examines early childhood development in the MENA region, documenting how investments in early learning programs can reduce inequality, improve school readiness, and generate significant long-term returns for individuals and economies.

title: The Case for Investing in Girls' Education
authors: Quentin Wodon, Claudio Montenegro, Hoa Nguyen, Adenike Onagoruwa
description: World Bank study estimating the global costs of not educating girls, finding that limited educational opportunities for girls cost countries between $15 and $30 trillion in lost lifetime productivity and human capital wealth.

title: Student Learning in South Asia: Challenges, Opportunities, and Policy Priorities
authors: Halil Dundar, Tara Beteille, Michelle Riboud, Anil Deolalikar
description: Comprehensive analysis of education quality in South Asia, documenting persistently low learning levels despite substantial enrollment gains and analyzing the teacher, governance, and financing challenges underlying the learning crisis.

title: COVID-19 and Education: The Lingering Effects of Unfinished Learning
description: Joint assessment finding that the COVID-19 pandemic increased learning poverty in low- and middle-income countries from 57% to an estimated 70%, with prolonged school closures causing learning losses equivalent to more than a year of schooling in many countries.

title: Education in Sub-Saharan Africa: Comparing Faith-Inspired, Private Secular, and Public Schools
description: Compares the performance of faith-inspired, private secular, and public schools across Sub-Saharan Africa, finding that faith-inspired schools serve a significant share of students, often in underserved areas, and frequently achieve comparable or better outcomes than public schools.

title: The Learning Generation: Investing in Education for a Changing World
authors: International Commission on Financing Global Education Opportunity
description: Report of the Education Commission chaired by Gordon Brown, proposing a financing compact to achieve a 'learning generation' by 2030, calling for increased domestic spending, reformed aid, and innovative financing mechanisms to address the learning crisis.

title: Learning Adjusted Years of Schooling: Defining a New Macro Measure of Education
authors: Noam Angrist, Simeon Djankov, Pinelopi Goldberg, Harry Anthony Patrinos
description: Introduces a harmonized measure of learning-adjusted years of schooling (LAYS) that combines enrollment and learning quality data, revealing that effective years of schooling are about half of enrolled years in many low-income countries.

title: What Matters Most for School Autonomy and Accountability: A Framework Paper
authors: Dina Abu-Ghaida, Sachiko Kataoka, Quentin Wodon
description: Presents a framework for understanding school-level autonomy and accountability mechanisms in developing countries, analyzing how decentralization, community participation, and accountability tools affect education quality.

title: Loud and Clear: Effective Language of Instruction Policies for Learning
description: Examines the evidence on language of instruction policies in developing countries, finding that children learn better when initially taught in their mother tongue and that early-exit transition to a second language can harm learning outcomes.

title: Global Education Monitoring Report 2023: Technology in Education
description: The GEM Report's critical appraisal of when, and whether, technology genuinely improves learning and equity.

title: The State of Global Learning Poverty: 2022 Update
authors: World Bank, UNESCO, UNICEF, FCDO, USAID, Gates Foundation
description: Estimates that 70% of 10-year-olds in low- and middle-income countries cannot read and understand a simple text.

title: Global Education Monitoring Report 2021/2: Non-State Actors
description: Examines the role of private and non-state provision in education and its implications for equity and the right to education.

title: Learning Losses from COVID-19 School Closures
description: 'The State of the Global Education Crisis'—a joint assessment of pandemic learning losses and recovery strategies.

title: Teaching at the Right Level: Evidence Review
description: Synthesis of the randomised evidence behind Pratham's TaRL approach to remediating foundational learning.

title: Cost-Effective Approaches to Improve Global Learning
authors: World Bank, FCDO, Building Evidence in Education
description: Ranks education interventions by their cost-effectiveness in delivering additional years of learning-adjusted schooling ('Smart Buys').

title: Girls' Education and Women's Empowerment
description: 'Missed Opportunities'—quantifies the large economic costs of not educating girls to secondary level.

title: Foundational Learning and the SDG 4 Agenda
description: Data and indicators tracking global progress toward inclusive and equitable quality education.

title: Improving Learning in Low- and Lower-Middle-Income Countries
description: The benefit-cost case for learning rather than spending. Primary education spending in low-income countries rose about $137 per student between 2000 and 2015, an 80 per cent real increase, with no change in average learning. Structured pedagogy and teaching at the right level return about $65 per $1.

title: Improving children's foundational learning through community-school participation: Experimental evidence from rural India
description: A trial in 400 Indian villages comparing community-only accountability against school-community collaboration. Both raise foundational literacy and numeracy; the collaborative arm pulls ahead only where parents actually visited the school.

title: Supporting learning in and out of school: Experimental evidence from India
description: A cross-cutting trial across 200 villages in Assam. Neither the in-school pedagogy component nor the community study groups moved learning alone; together they raised maths by 0.11 SD and language by 0.09 SD. An argument about complementarity rather than about either component.

title: The effectiveness of technology‐supported personalised learning in low‐ and middle‐income countries: A meta‐analysis
authors: Louis Major, Gill A. Francis, Maria Tsapali
description: 16 trials, 53,029 learners aged 6 to 15. Overall effect 0.18 SD; approaches that genuinely adapt to a learner's level reach 0.35 SD, while those that only personalise feedback or interests do not. The distinction the word personalised usually hides.

title: Improving learning outcomes for out-of-school children: evidence from a randomized evaluation of an accelerated learning program in Liberia
description: Liberia records 2.2 learning-adjusted years of schooling, among the lowest measured anywhere. A ten-month accelerated programme across 100 communities brings out-of-school children up to the learning level of children in government schools.

title: Digital personalised learning to improve literacy and numeracy outcomes: a randomised controlled trial in Kenyan pre-primary classrooms
description: 1,955 pre-primary learners across 291 Kenyan government schools over 13 months, 0.53 SD from baseline. Worth reading for the decay after midline, which the authors attribute to running out of suitable content rather than to the method failing.

title: Pedagogical features of interactive apps for effective learning of foundational skills
authors: Bethany Huntington, James Goulding, Nicola J. Pitchford
description: Compares the five Global Learning XPRIZE apps deployed to 2,041 out-of-school children in 172 Tanzanian villages. Six features separate the winners; free play is not one of them.

title: The impact of a participatory intervention to improve learning outcomes and reduce school-based discrimination and community stigma in primary rural schools of Afghanistan: A cluster control randomized trial
description: 83 schools across three Afghan provinces, 2,519 children. Life skills, self-efficacy and reading literacy all improve, effects rise with dose, and girls gain more than boys. One of the few learning trials run in an active crisis setting.
